title: Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Contact Lens Used in Trabeculectomy

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License'; no version number or licence URL given in the XML)

indication: primary angle-closure glaucoma (acute and chronic) not controlled with maximal-tolerated medical therapy or after acute angle closure, adults > 18 years without diabetes; fornix-based trabeculectomy by one surgeon; prospective randomized two-arm study (Jinan, China)

groups.description: Group 1: fornix-based trabeculectomy followed by a soft bandage contact lens (14 mm), the experimental adjunct; 100 eyes of 100 patients (tab1!R1C2 header)
Group 2: fornix-based trabeculectomy without contact lens (standard care); 100 eyes of 100 patients (tab1!R1C3 header)

series.baseline_label: Table 2 row 'Basal IOP' (same cell text as Table 1 'Basal IOP (mmHg; mean ± SD)', tab1!R6C2)
series.notes: mean ± SD (column header); rows Day 1, Week 1, Week 2, Month 1, Month 3, Month 6, Month 12; per-visit n not reported (4 Group-1 patients lost to follow-up, ordinary attrition); the Discussion states that IOP was measured over the contact lens with Goldmann tonometry

series.baseline_label: Table 2 row 'Basal IOP' (same cell text as Table 1 'Basal IOP (mmHg; mean ± SD)', tab1!R6C3)
series.notes: mean ± SD (column header); rows Day 1, Week 1, Week 2, Month 1, Month 3, Month 6, Month 12; per-visit n not reported (5 Group-2 patients lost to follow-up, ordinary attrition)

exclusions.reason: medication numbers are not IOP series in schema 1.0.0; noted only

exclusions.what: Table 5 complications and postsurgical interventions (including bleb needling counts)
qualified and complete success (life-table / Kaplan-Meier, Figures 1-2)
exclusions.reason: success proportions / Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': inclusion required PACG not controlled with maximal-tolerated medical therapy (or after acute angle closure), the preoperative number of antiglaucoma medications is tabulated (tab1!R5), and patients were told to stop their preoperative antiglaucoma medications after surgery; no washout described.

Tonometer: Goldmann applanation tonometer (Haag-Streit AT900) named for the preoperative data; the Discussion states that postoperative IOP was measured with Goldmann tonometry over the contact lens in the lens group (method 'goldmann').
Day 1, Week 1 and Week 2 converted as 1/30.4375, 7/30.4375 and 14/30.4375 months (rounded to 4 decimals).
Trabeculectomy technique follows Zhang et al. (reference 15); antimetabolite use is not stated in this article.
Roles: the bandage contact lens is the investigational adjunct declared as the experimental arm (randomized), so Group 1 is 'treated' and Group 2 'control'.
Antiglaucoma medication numbers at baseline and 1/3/6/12 months are tabulated in Table 3 (not extracted).
